evidence.claim: Connecticut’s Route 169 byway winds past stone walls, colonial houses and meetinghouses, with maple and pine stands and glacial boulders scattered through fields.
evidence.quote: This byway winds through history, passing colonial homesteads, churches, stone walls, meeting houses, and private schools as it connects classic New England towns. Views include maple and pine stands and glacially deposited rocks and boulders that lie strewn throughout fields.

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration lists this National Scenic Byway as 32 miles and allows an hour for the drive, or a full day with visits.
evidence.quote: National Scenic Byway • Connecticut Length 32 mi / 51.5 km Time to Allow Take one hour to drive without stopping or one full day to visit places along the byway.

evidence.claim: The Norwich and Woodstock Turnpike began as a private toll road incorporated in 1801; its corporation dissolved in 1846.
evidence.quote: The Norwich and Woodstock Turnpike was a private toll road incorporated in 1801 connecting the city of Norwich to the town center of Woodstock. The corporation was dissolved in 1846.
